facts.raw_span: An 18-month-old girl was brought for evaluation of a swelling in her left medial thigh
the mass had enlarged gradually and was painless, with no history of trauma or infection
a firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
no signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh, extending toward the inguinal area
The lesion exhibited internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, displacing the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion
it abutted the proximal femoral bone but did not erode it
An MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations and no encasement of neurovascular structures

concepts.why: The mass is described as a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, which is consistent with a lipoma.
The mass is described as a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations, which is consistent with a lipoblastoma.
The mass is described as displacing the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion, which could be consistent with a hemangioma.
The mass is described as a firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, which could be consistent with a fibromatosis.
The mass is described as a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, which could be consistent with a myxoid liposarcoma.
The mass is described as abutting the proximal femoral bone but not eroding it, which could be consistent with a neurofibroma.

The mass is described as a firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, which could be consistent with a desmoid tumor.
